subject: Hosted vs Dedicated: Latency/Throughput follow-up
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Priya Reddy <priya.reddy@avatech.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, 10 May 2026 15:20:00 -0700
Subject: Hosted vs Dedicated: Latency/Throughput follow-up

Hi Priya —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery call and a couple of clarifying questions so we can recommend the best deployment path (Hosted API vs Dedicated capacity vs Private VPC).

Recap of your use case:
- Product: in-app real-time support chat (short-form prompts, ~200-400 tokens per request)
- Model preference: open Llama2-13B (quantized) or similar
- Primary constraints: p99 latency / user experience and predictable throughput during business hours
- Data residency: US-only; no current on-prem requirement

What we heard re: traffic (please correct if I misunderstood):
- Steady-state QPS: ~60-80
- Peak spikes: up to ~140-160 QPS during product launches (short 15-30 minute bursts)
- Target p99 latency: <= 300ms (ideally ~250ms)
- Concurrent active users during peaks: ~50-70

Questions for sizing and recommendation:
1) Can you confirm the 95th/99th percentile token lengths (we estimated 200-400 tokens above)?
2) Are spikes predictable (scheduled launches) or more organic?
3) Any hard procurement/PO timeline we should factor into trial sizing?

Initial guidance: based on the targets above, Hosted API can be sufficient for most steady-state traffic if coupled with KV caching and request batching; however, for consistent p99 <=250ms under 140-160 QPS spikes, Dedicated reserved capacity (or a hybrid hosted + dedicated burst policy) typically provides the most predictable SLOs.

Next steps I propose:
- You share the traffic projection spreadsheet (a stub is attached for convenience)
- Quick 30-minute tech deep dive with Dev to validate exact latency/throughput numbers and run a preliminary capacity calc
- We can provide a short Dedicated trial quote (1-2 week proof-of-concept) to validate p99 targets under realistic load

Proposed times for the technical deep dive: Tue 5/12 10:00-10:30am PT or Wed 5/13 1:00-1:30pm PT — tell me what works and I’ll calendar invite.

Attachments: [Attachment: avatech_traffic_projections.xlsx (spreadsheet)]

Thanks —
Marissa
Sr. Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com | (415) 555-0198

Marissa —

Thanks for the recap, exactly the right level of detail. A few clarifications and I attached our traffic projection spreadsheet as requested.

Clarifications:
- Token lengths: median ~180 tokens, 95th ~420 tokens (we see some longer threads when agents paste context)
- Spikes: a mix — about half are predictable (planned feature launches) and half organic (unexpected demand). Peak bursts historically ~15-30 minutes.
- Typical concurrency mapping: at 140 QPS we see ~60-70 concurrent active sessions
- Compliance: US-only data residency is a hard requirement; SOC 2 is expected as part of procurement but no additional encryption/HSM needs today

Procurement timeline: we’re targeting a procurement decision within 2 weeks if the technical validation confirms latency targets. We have budget flexibility to do a reserved commitment if ROI is clear.

Attached: avatech_traffic_projections.xlsx (contains hour-by-hour QPS and percentile token length columns)

We’re open to a Dedicated trial if that’s your recommendation for hitting p99 <=250ms during spikes. Please loop in Dev for the deep dive — Tue 5/12 10am PT works for us.

—Priya

priya.reddy@avatech.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Re: Hosted vs Dedicated: Latency/Throughput follow-up

Priya —

Appreciate the quick turnaround and thanks for the spreadsheet — that helps a lot. Based on the numbers and your p99 <=250ms requirement, here’s our recommended path and rationale:

Recommendation (short): Dedicated reserved capacity with burst/overflow to hosted API (hybrid routing).

Why:
- Predictability: Dedicated provides consistent GPU allocation which makes hitting p99 SLOs under bursty peaks far simpler vs relying solely on hosted autoscaling during short spikes.
- Control: You can tune batching, KV cache sizing, and kernel/quantization profiles on Dedicated for lower variance latency at your model and token lengths.
- Cost: For sustained baseline QPS (60-80) + regular spikes to ~150 QPS, a modest reserved pool with a short burst policy is often more cost-effective than overprovisioning hosted autoscale. We’ll run a TCO calc in the tech deep dive.

Alternative if you want to delay commit: start on Hosted API with aggressive caching (prefix caching for common prompts) and run a staged load test to establish whether p99 holds during spikes. If it fails, migrate to Dedicated (we support smooth rollouts).

Next proposals:
1) Confirm deep dive: Tue 5/12 10:00am PT — Dev will run through model perf/kv cache strategy and preliminary capacity numbers.
2) We’ll prepare a draft Dedicated trial plan (1 week with monitoring hooks + success criteria based on p99 and token cost) and a back-of-envelope price/commit estimate for your finance team.

I’ll calendar invite for Tue and include a short pre-read (capacity assumptions + metrics we’ll collect). Let us know any other stakeholders to add (e.g., infra/procurement).

Thanks —
Marissa
Sr. Account Executive | Redwood Inference
